authored_lights.softbox_fit: RE-HUNG for this component (r8): --softbox-y 0.46 (height; hard ceiling — past Y_low ≈ GHH the glass edges stop seeing the box and the band collapses to a blob), --softbox-depth 0.45 (thickness), --softbox-z 0.96 (throw; the ∪ spans 68 px at 1.9 and 151 px at 0.96), 16 W. The panel's fit does not transfer: that is a perspective rig where a fixture images at half size, this is ORTHO where it images ~1:1. The ortho camera re-parks itself 1.0 behind the softbox so it can never appear in frame.

ratified_physics.fastener_placement: corner screws sit at the midpoint of the rim along the diagonal; the 45° point of a superellipse-n corner is r·2^(-1/n) from the arc centre, so the midpoint constant is k = 1 - 2^(-1/n). The circle constant dragged it inland ~23 px on the n=4 CRT and ~4 px on the n=3 LCD (exactly Sam's "majorly CRT, minorly LCD"). Second contributor: OUTER_R = GLASS_CR + BW·0.4 — a big outer radius widens the rim at the corner and drags the true midpoint inward on its own. Four rounds (r2, r4, r5) before the superellipse was the answer (r6); the same fix landed in panel_scene.py.
ratified_physics.glass_profile: z = b·(1 - t^roll)^peak, t = (u²+v²)/2. Under the ortho camera the glass point (x,y) mirrors the source-plane point Y = y·m(t), m = 1 + 2·b·L·(-f')/GHH² ≥ 1 — wherever the glass is steeper the band is pushed DOWN. A plain paraboloid does nothing (a quadric mirror is an AFFINE position→direction map, so a straight source stays a straight band at every depth); only curvature VARIATION bends it. RATIFIED: CRT roll 1 / peak 4 — curvature in the CENTRE, flat rim, so the band's ends ride at m ≈ 1 and arc INTO the top corners (Sam's ∪ ruling). LCD flat, roll 1 / peak 1.
ratified_physics.band_rows: measured on the raw _refl.png (where the composed image puts them — the treatments composite refl at the raw uv), lower edge at 12/50/88 % of aperture width, rows growing downward on the 549-row aperture: CRT r7 184/142/185 (∩) → r8 113/205/115 (∪, ends 91 px ABOVE centre; 54/53 at 4 %/96 %, symmetric to 2 px). LCD 206/206/206, straight and unmoved.
ratified_physics.coat_roughness: 0.05 — 0.17 smears the reflection into a shapeless shaft, 0.10 keeps it, 0.05 reads crisp; it cannot go razor-CG because the source is a big softbox whose penumbra is geometric, not coat-borne. Judged on the COMPOSED screen; on the raw layer every value looks fine.
ratified_physics.glare_strength: 1.0 — refl is baked at final intensity and the treatments composite it as a straight `col += refl`, so 1.0 is both the identity for that composite and the value the reflection tuning was judged at.
ratified_physics.glare_history: the AUTHORED glare disc (r1-r4) was cut, re-textured (a rectangular softbox bar 'reads CGI' → a round disc), halved twice, aperture-fraction repositioned and finally nixed to zero on Sam's r4 verdict; the layer came back at r7 as a REAL aimed env reflection, which is what ratified.

A fresh LCD bake through the r8 generator was verified against the cached r7 one — _refl max 1 luma on 42 px of 786 k, _vig max 2, manifest byte-identical — against a renderer noise floor of 134 luma measured on the UNTOUCHED bezel pass (GPU/denoiser nondeterminism). The plate then composed the LCD from the r7 cache, so its p45 tile IS its p43 tile. These are the ratified pixels.
